sections.h2: How do I contact the Edgecombe County Register of Deeds?
sections.html:
This office keeps the county's land records along with births, deaths, marriages, military discharges, notary files and maps. The county page lists (252) 641-7924, so phone ahead for counter hours and the street address.

The office says three state bodies govern it: the Legislature, the Secretary of State and North Carolina Vital Records. Voters elect each county's register every two years under G.S. 161-1. Tarboro is the county seat in a rural county, roughly an hour east of Raleigh, that the county describes as built on farming with some advanced manufacturing.

When you sell an Edgecombe County house, your signed deed lands here, usually sent by the closing attorney. The next sections cover the charges and local quirks.

sections.h2: What price list does the Edgecombe register of deeds follow?
sections.html:
The office lists $26.00 for a deed of up to 15 pages and $4.00 per later page, with its excise tax line printed as $1.00 per $500.00. The table below follows the office's fee schedule PDF.

Edgecombe County register of deeds fee schedule, reproduced from the county PDF

The sheet promises same day processing of filings and requests, and asks mail customers to include a stamped, self addressed return envelope.

sections.h2: Why does Edgecombe County ask for a tax certification on deeds?
sections.html:
A county resolution requires every deed to carry the Tax Collector's certification before recording, per the fee schedule, with one way around it. The deed can instead bear a statement that a licensed North Carolina attorney prepared it and that the closing attorney will deliver any delinquent taxes to the county tax collector from the closing proceeds.

An attorney drafting your deed can add that line. If you prepare a deed yourself, stop at the Tax Collector first and request the certification.

  • Attorney route: the preparer statement satisfies the resolution, and back taxes come out of your proceeds.
  • Do it yourself route: obtain the certification before bringing the deed to the register.

sections.h2: Can an Edgecombe County deed be sent in electronically?
sections.html:
Yes. The county's E-Recording page names Simplifile as the vendor and also points to CSC eRecording Solutions. Law firms and title agents with an account can transmit the deed without a courier.

A seller with no account should ask the closing attorney to file it. Paper filings follow the state filing standards that the Real Estate page posts as a PDF, next to an Assumed Name form and property check instructions.

sections.h2: What must never appear in a document I submit for recording?
sections.html:
Leave out Social Security, taxpayer ID, driver's license, state ID, passport, bank account, credit card and debit card numbers, plus PINs and passwords. The county's notice cites G.S. 132-1.10(g)(1) and permits such a number only when a law or court order demands it, or when only the last four digits remain.

Filed documents join the official county records, so read yours before signing and ask the preparer to strip anything sensitive.

sections.h2: How does a deed recording affect farm or timber land here?
sections.html:
The county treats the recording date as the transfer date for Present Use Value purposes. A buyer who wants land to stay in the use value program has 60 days from that date to file a new application.

The program page also says the new owner takes on deferred taxes, including those from years before the sale, and that leaving the program makes the current year plus three earlier years payable with interest. A seller with such land should ask the Tax Assessor for its status before listing or accepting an offer.

  • Farm use needs 10 cultivated acres, and forest use needs 20 forested acres plus a management plan.
  • Farm income must average $1000 a year across the last three years.
  • A sale to an owner who cannot qualify can take the land out of the program.

sections.h2: How are vital record copies priced at this office?
sections.html:
Each certified copy of a birth, death or marriage certificate costs $10. The office takes online orders through Permitium/AIS, which adds a $3.35 convenience fee plus card fees, and it also accepts a mailed application.

The Vital Records page says birth and death files begin in October 1913 and marriage files in 1867.

sections.h2: How do property taxes connect to a deed in Edgecombe County?
sections.html:
The Tax Collector's office bills and collects real estate, personal property and vehicle tax for the county, 14 fire districts, one drainage district and eight towns. It also prepares statements of taxes due for attorneys and real estate professionals, which a closing attorney can request before a sale closes.

Questions about taxes paid or owed go to (252) 641-7810, and questions about a value go to the Tax Assessor at (252) 641-7855. Our Edgecombe County property tax guide covers rates, listing and appeals.

sections.h2: Which county office records a deed for a Rocky Mount or Tarboro home?
sections.html:
Recording follows the county where the land lies. A Tarboro house, the county seat, goes to the Edgecombe County office, and so does the Edgecombe side of Rocky Mount. The county's own description notes that Rocky Mount is divided between Nash and Edgecombe counties and is the largest municipality here, so check which side of the line your parcel sits on before you send the deed.

The excise tax statute adds a rule for a single parcel that crosses a county line: the tax is paid to the register in the county holding the greater share of the value. Edgecombe's tax rate table lists ten municipalities, including Princeville, Pinetops, Whitakers, Speed, Leggett, Conetoe, Macclesfield and Sharpsburg, so a parcel in a small town still needs its county confirmed.

Ask your closing attorney to confirm the parcel number and the county before the signing appointment, since the fee schedule's same day processing only helps when the paper reaches the right office.

sections.h2: What housing facts does the Census report for Edgecombe County?
sections.html:
Edgecombe County is small and rural. QuickFacts gives the following snapshot.

  • 49,121 residents in the July 2025 estimate, living in 23,604 housing units.
  • 60.8% of homes occupied by their owners, with a median value of $125,100.
  • Median household income of $51,265 and median rent of $858.
  • Adults 65 or older make up 23.1% of residents.
  • 53 building permits issued in 2025.

Recording fees are fixed by statute, so a $125,100 house pays the same page charge as a far costlier one. The excise tax is the line that follows the price.

faqs.q: Is there a fee to record a mortgage release in Edgecombe County?
faqs.a: No. The fee schedule lists a satisfaction at no fee, so releasing a mortgage at closing adds no recording charge.

faqs.q: What is the Edgecombe County excise tax rate?
faqs.a: The county prints $1.00 per $500.00. State law makes the seller pay it to the register of deeds before recording, and the office collects it along with the deed.

faqs.q: Does Edgecombe County record a deed that lacks a tax certification?
faqs.a: Only if the deed carries the attorney preparer statement. Otherwise the county resolution requires the Tax Collector's certification, and the statement must say a licensed North Carolina attorney prepared the deed and the closing attorney will pay delinquent taxes from proceeds.

faqs.q: How do I get a certified birth or death certificate in Edgecombe County?
faqs.a: Order online through Permitium/AIS or mail the application for certified copy. Each copy costs $10, and the online route adds a $3.35 convenience fee plus card fees.

faqs.q: Does the Edgecombe County register accept electronic filing?
faqs.a: Yes. The county accepts e-recording through Simplifile and lists CSC eRecording Solutions as another route, so ask your closing attorney or title company to submit the deed.
